sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4m in FY2016 [F1] to $14,342.9m in FY2025 [F10][F198]; the FY2018 and FY2019 recasts [R2] do not affect those endpoints.

Revenue rose 89.1% to a $16,071.7m peak in FY2021 [D241][F6] and fell 24.3% in FY2022 [D292]; REGEN-COV US sales went from $5,828.0m [S48] to $0.0m [S49], and the FY2022 filing says the 2021 sales did not recur [P33].
Operating margin peaked at 55.7% in FY2021 [F26] and has fallen four years running to 24.9% [F30][R1].
Collaboration revenue was 51.1% of FY2025 revenue [D521], and Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits, $5,241.6m [S52], added 9.3pp to growth [D592].
The filing attributes that line's 33.6% rise [D591] to higher profits from increased Dupixent sales [P9].
Total revenue grew only 1.0% [D440] as US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% [D577], a 14.2pp drag [D578].
The filing cites lower volumes from competition, bevacizumab share loss and the move to EYLEA HD, plus a lower net selling price [P10][D577].
Operating income fell 10.3% [D441] while operating costs rose 5.4% [D457] on 1.0% revenue growth [D440], so profit moved against revenue.
Diluted EPS rose 8.2% [D444] against 2.1% net income growth [D442], with diluted shares down 5.6% to 108.6m [D459][X127].
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% [F30] is the window low [D749], against a window median of 34.6% [D751] and a high of 55.7% [D750].
R&D cut the margin by 4.7pp [D465] while R&D grew 14.0% [D455], and SG&A added 2.0pp [D466] after an 8.6% fall [D456].
The FY2025 filing ties the SG&A fall to lower charitable contributions to the Good Days fund [P5][D456]; no cited passage explains the R&D rise [D455].

The window's largest move, FY2022, cut operating margin 16.7pp [D305], with R&D taking 11.4pp [D318] and SG&A 6.0pp [D319]; the filing ties the 15.9% SG&A rise [D308] to headcount and Libtayo commercialization from July 2022 [P34].
Net margin of 31.4% [F50] sits 6.5pp above operating margin [F30], with other income of $1,652.8m [X117] that the cited passages do not explain.
FY2025 operating cash flow was 1.11x net income [D428] and free cash flow 0.91x [D429], against a window median of 0.88x [D763].
Capex was 6.3% of revenue [D424] and 1.65x D&A [D430], while the 28.4% free cash flow margin [D425] sat above its 26.4% median [D757].

Conversion fell to 0.75x in FY2020 [D181] as receivables rose partly on extended payment terms for EYLEA customers during COVID-19 [P51], lifting days sales outstanding to 134 [D191] from 97 in FY2019 [D140].
Net cash was $16,879.9m at FY2025 [D434], 117.7% of revenue [D435], ranking at the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers [D780] against a peer median of -50.7% [D781].
Net cash rose from $15,928.2m in FY2024 [D385] as cash and investments of $18,865.8m [D432] outran debt of $1,985.9m [D433].
FY2025 buybacks of $3,438.6m [X137] and dividends of $370.3m [X140] totalled $3,808.9m [D436], or 93.3% of free cash flow [D437], while diluted shares fell 5.6% to 108.6m [D459][X127].
Shareholder returns now absorb nearly all free cash flow, leaving little cushion if it weakens.
The margin squeeze is the most persistent flag: operating margin has fallen four years running [R1], to 24.9% [F30] from 55.7% [F26].
The FY2024 filing ties SG&A growth of 12.3% [D407] to EYLEA HD launch costs [P14].
Costs are growing faster than revenue, so recovery depends on sales growth that FY2025 did not show, with revenue up 1.0% [D440].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% in FY2025 [D577], and their share of revenue dropped from 58.2% in FY2020 [D561] to 19.2% [D576].
The filing cites lower volumes and a lower net selling price, including share loss to compounded bevacizumab [P10][D577].
The combined US EYLEA and EYLEA HD subtotal fell to $4,384.7m [S46] from $5,968.2m [S45], so the HD transition has not yet offset the erosion.
Operating margin: a FY2026 10-K margin below the 24.9% window low [F30][D749] would confirm the compression, while one above the 34.6% median [D751] would reverse it.
US EYLEA and EYLEA HD subtotal: a FY2026 10-K figure below $4,384.7m [S46] would confirm further erosion, while one above FY2024's $5,968.2m [S45] would show the transition holding.
Free cash flow cover: free cash flow below $3,808.9m [D436] in the FY2026 10-K would mean FY2025-level buybacks and dividends are no longer covered by it.
